tweet_summary: A pro-Democratic meme image presenting a fabricated 1998 People-Magazine 'quote' from Donald Trump calling Republicans 'the dumbest group of voters', shared earnestly ('Keepin' it real!').
why_note_decision: The quote is a long-debunked fabrication. People Magazine combed its archive and found no such interview or quote; the meme has been repeatedly debunked by Snopes, FactCheck.org, PolitiFact, Full Fact, and Newsweek since 2015. The Fox News reference is itself an anachronism (Fox News was little-known and not yet partisan-coded in 1998). The tweet has 1.17M impressions and is being shared as a real quote, not a self-aware joke. A note labeling it fabricated is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note clearly says the People Magazine 1998 quote is fabricated and was never said by Trump, citing at least one credible fact-check (Snopes / PolitiFact / FactCheck.org / Full Fact). The note must not equivocate ('appears to be fake', 'no evidence found') — sources are definitive. FAIL if the note instead claims the quote is genuine, or if the bot declines (this is a clear fabricated-quote case worth correcting).
reference_note: This 1998 People Magazine quote is fabricated. People Magazine searched its archive and found no record of any 1998 Trump interview or this quote. Fact-checkers including Snopes, PolitiFact and FactCheck.org have repeatedly debunked it since 2015. https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/republicans-dumbest-group-of-voters/ https://www.factcheck.org/2015/11/bogus-meme-targets-trump/ https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2018/dec/18/blog-posting/no-donald-trump-did-not-call-republican-voters-dum/

original_unhelpful_note.text: This quote is not genuine and was not said by Donald Trump in a 1998 People Magazine interview. The magazine has no record of it. Fact-checkers confirm it's fabricated.    https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/1998-trump-people-quote/  https://www.foxnews.com/entertainment/bette-midler-blasted-for-tweeting-fake-trump-quote-bashing-republicans-and-fox-news  https://www.breitbart.com/entertainment/2019/06/03/bette-midler-blasted-after-tweeting-fake-donald-trump-quote
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Substantively correct content, but raters flagged sources (Fox/Breitbart entertainment columns) as unreliable/biased. A stronger note would lead with Snopes/FactCheck/PolitiFact and drop the Fox/Breitbart links.

fact_check.notes: Fabricated quote first surfaced 2015. People Magazine has no record. Anachronism: Fox News was not partisan-coded in 1998.

importance.lens_rationale: Political misinformation at 1M+ impressions; fake-quote memes erode epistemic trust on all sides. Catching fabricated-quote images is a core notewriter capability.
